vote_a.rationale: migration agent gives immigration assistance without being a lawyer; nearest legal-support code

vote_b.rationale: Registered migration agent gives regulated immigration advice without being a lawyer; no dedicated O*NET code exists.

rationale: Pool string: "principal migration agent" (VIC, 1 member). An Australian registered migration agent (MARA-registered) gives immigration assistance in their own right — advising on visa eligibility, preparing and lodging applications, representing clients before the Department and the tribunal. "Principal" is seniority within a migration practice, so per rule 1 the occupation is "migration agent". Coder A's 23-2011.00 fails on its verified O*NET definition, "Assist lawyers by investigating facts, preparing legal documents, or researching legal precedent": a registered migration agent is not a lawyer's assistant, and since March 2021 practising lawyers are in fact excluded from the Australian migration-agent scheme, so the modal migration agent is a non-lawyer practitioner working autonomously. O*NET has no detailed code for immigration consultant/migration agent (checked /find/quick for "immigration", "immigration consultant" and "migration agent" — no quick match, only Lawyers/Paralegals/Compliance/CBP by keyword relevance). The work is nonetheless legal-services work in SOC minor group 23-2000 Legal Support Workers, so the verified residual 23-2099.00 ("All legal support workers not listed separately") is the correct landing spot. Coder B upheld. Not unknown: the string names a determinate, regulated occupation; only the detailed code is missing from the taxonomy, which is exactly what the residual is for.

vote_a.rationale: manager at a government agency, function unspecified

vote_b.rationale: Manager in the national welfare-payments agency directs social service delivery.

rationale: Pool string: "manager with Centrelink" (VIC, 1 member). Centrelink is the Australian government agency delivering social security payments and related services (Services Australia, formerly DHS) — a public social-service/benefits program, not a general commercial enterprise. Verified 11-9151.00 definition: "Plan, direct, or coordinate the activities of a social service program or community outreach organization. Oversee the program or organization's budget and policies regarding participant involvement, program requirements, and benefits" — the "program requirements and benefits" clause is a direct fit for income-support administration, and US public-assistance office managers are the analogue of the Australian role. Coder A's 11-1021.00 is by its own verified definition the residual for managers whose "duties are too diverse and general in nature to be classified in any one functional area of management or administration"; here a functional area (social services) is named by the employer, so the functional code beats the residual. Rule 2 (modal member) supports this: the modal Centrelink manager runs service delivery of social security programs, not IT/HR/finance. Coder B upheld, with the honest caveat that the string does not state the management level (a service-centre manager could arguably be 43-1011.00 First-Line Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers), but "manager" is taken at face value per rule 1.
note: Rubric-driven, not title-driven: the split turns on rule 2 (modal member of the category) and on the residual-vs-functional-code convention, not on ambiguity in the phrase itself. The one soft spot is that 'manager with Centrelink' fixes the employer, not the function, so the domain code rests on the modal-member assumption.
